anytime_rule: max_{s<=t} log BF_s >= log(1/alpha); no horizon calibration

alpha_prior.note: inf is the equal-tail spike limit, so the existing bayes_shared rule is one component of this mixture.

bayes_dirichlet.component: f_{Delta,alpha}(r) = r**(Delta/(1-Delta)) + K E_q[r**(1/(Delta q)-1)] with q ~ Beta(alpha, (K-1)alpha) the tail marginal of a Dirichlet(alpha,...,alpha) tail on K = V-1 coordinates.

normalisation.note: Components are exactly normalised analytically. The reported tokenwise mass includes both the inner component transform and the outer prior-mixture lookup. It is a numerical quadrature diagnostic for the configured tables, not a certificate that interpolation error is one-sided for every pivot or configuration.

midpoint_log_ratio.reference: direct evaluation of the same frozen component mixture; this isolates outer interpolation error

bayes_dirichlet.why_gumbel_only: The inverse limiting alternative depends on Delta alone, so a prior on the tail shape is inert for it by construction.

bayes_gumbel: Exact spike-family f1(r|Delta), integrated over the data-generating Uniform(0.001,0.5) prior; tokenwise independent Delta.

midpoint_log_density.reference: direct evaluation of the same frozen Gauss-Legendre deficit quadrature

bayes_inverse: Large-V triangular f1(d|Delta) of Li et al. (2025), analytically integrated over Uniform(0.001,0.5), divided by the exact finite-V null density.
bayes_shared: For the shared-Delta sensitivity scenario, integrates the joint document likelihood integral prod_t f1(y_t|Delta) pi(Delta)dDelta.

bayes_uniontail.hierarchy_scope: This records the hierarchies evaluated, not a general claim that tokenwise mixtures cannot improve power.
bayes_uniontail.why_gumbel_only: The working inverse limiting alternative depends on Delta alone.
bayes_uniontail.component: A union of a full-width Dirichlet tail-shape branch and an equal-weight live-tail-width branch restricted to J < V-1. The width component is f_{Delta,J}(r) = r**(Delta/(1-Delta)) + J*r**(J/Delta-1). The shape component uses the tabulated psi_alpha transform.

tail_width_prior.family: uniform on the configured ladder strictly below V-1
tail_width_prior.note: The equal-tail atom (alpha=inf, J=V-1) belongs to the shape branch. It is excluded from the width branch to avoid counting the full-width atom twice.

normalisation.note: Both branches integrate to one analytically. The width formula is closed form; the shape implementation interpolates a transform table. Tokenwise scoring, when requested, also uses outer lookups. Numerical mass and node-sensitivity checks are not certificates that the evaluated densities have mass at most one. The exact test-martingale result requires conditional null validity and analytic or certified normalized evaluation; it is not asserted for these interpolated implementations.

prior_fingerprint.family: union of the Dirichlet tail-shape and tail-width families

containment_check.note: Recorded discrepancy for the equal-tail atom in the interpolated shape branch; not an exact arithmetic identity.

outer_tokenwise_lookup_validation_proven.note: Newly computed using the recorded production lookup configuration; no original document arrays or estimates were regenerated.

metadata_correction.scope: Description corrected from the stored union prior fingerprint; numerical results unchanged.

calibration: Independent exact-null Monte Carlo. Fixed-horizon rule is score>c plus a randomized score=c boundary chosen to target alpha.

diagnostic_scores_not_from_the_paper.definition: log f^sp_Delta(r) with f^sp_Delta(r) = r**(Delta/(1-Delta)) + (V-1) r**((V-1)/Delta - 1), the exact data-generating spike density at a single fixed Delta; f0(r)=1 so this is the log likelihood ratio.
diagnostic_scores_not_from_the_paper.purpose: This diagnostic is not among the scores evaluated by Li et al. (2025). It uses the data-generating spike family with one fixed Delta and no Bayesian averaging, isolating the contribution of component-family choice relative to averaging over Delta. The h*_gum,Delta as evaluated by Li et al. (2025) instead uses the least-favorable family.

important_reproduction_note: The written specification of Li et al. (2025) makes Delta_t iid across tokens with an equal tail. The commit-pinned accompanying simulation snapshot instead samples one Delta per document and redraws random normalized-uniform tail probabilities at each token. This benchmark reports the written specification and a shared-Delta, equal-tail sensitivity that isolates the consequential dependence change.
official_code_note: Commit-pinned upstream snapshot used only to document the simulator and reference-score conventions attributed to Li et al. (2025). This repository's provenance.json separately identifies the code that produced the Bayesian benchmark artifacts.

boundary_randomization.aggregate_rate_note: CSV power is the conditional expectation greater + gamma*equal; the persisted indicators are one reproducible realization of that reported randomized-boundary procedure.
boundary_randomization.coupling: The same auxiliary U_i is reused for document i by every method in a scenario/scheme/horizon cell; cells have separate addressable SeedSequence streams independent of pivot RNGs.

per_document_indicators.rule: score > c or (score == c and U_i < gamma) at each method's own calibrated fixed-horizon cutoff c and boundary probability gamma

primary_scenario.delta: Delta_t iid Uniform(0.001, 0.5) at every token
primary_scenario.inverse_H1: exact finite-V inverse-CDF watermark for equal-tail spike
primary_scenario.name: paper_text_iid_delta_equal_tail

shared_delta_sensitivity.delta: one Delta ~ Uniform(0.001,0.5) shared by the document
shared_delta_sensitivity.name: shared_delta_equal_tail_sensitivity
shared_delta_sensitivity.purpose: Isolates the commit-pinned simulation snapshot's document-shared deficit while retaining the equal-tail spike stated by Li et al. (2025).

trgof.atom_at_zero: The empty truncated index set gives the statistic an atom at zero, most of it at short prefixes. It is calibrated on the same exact-null sample, at the same nominal alpha, with the same randomized score == c boundary as every other rule; no special case.
trgof.citation_title: Robust Detection of Watermarks for Large Language Models Under Human Edits

gumbel_p_value.attribution: The authors'. Their released implementation applies Tr-GoF to the Gumbel-max pivot only.
gumbel_p_value.definition: p = 1 - Y, exactly uniform under the null

trgof.implementation: code/trgof.py, a term-by-term reimplementation of the authors' released compute_score, kept as the single owner of the statistic so every caller in this study shares it.

inverse_p_value.attribution: OURS, not the authors'. Li et al. (2024) define no p-value for the inverse-transform pivot and their released code does not apply Tr-GoF to it. This extension is labelled as ours wherever it is reported.
inverse_p_value.definition: p = F_0(d), the exact finite-vocabulary null CDF of the inverse-transform pivot |U - eta(I)|; small d is the evidence direction, so the one-sided p-value is the CDF rather than its complement.
inverse_p_value.exact_null_note: The null is the exact finite-M law at M = 1000, whose density is piecewise constant, so the p-values are uniform at finite vocabulary rather than only asymptotically.

trgof.no_anytime_row: Tr-GoF is a fixed-horizon statistic, not an e-process, so it is reported only under the fixed-horizon calibrated rule.
trgof.not_a_token_sum: The statistic sorts the p-values of the whole prefix, so it is not additive over tokens and cannot be accumulated with a cumulative sum. It is recomputed from scratch at every reported prefix, like the shared-latent Bayes rules, and is therefore not a member of GUMBEL_METHODS or INVERSE_METHODS.
trgof.s_note: s = 2 is Higher Criticism, the index the authors' figures lead with.
trgof.s_sensitivity_note: The authors' simulation code sweeps [2.0, 1.5, 1.0, 0.5, 0.0]. Only s = 2.0 is evaluated as a rule here, to keep one Tr-GoF row per scheme in tables that are already large; the remaining indices are recorded as this sensitivity grid and were not run.
trgof.statistic: S_n(s) = n * max_t K_s(t/n, p_(t)) over the sorted prefix p-values p_(1) <= ... <= p_(n), with K_s the Cressie-Read phi-divergence between the empirical and null occupancy of each order statistic.
trgof.truncation: The maximum is taken over the truncated, one-sided index set p_(t) >= 1/n and t/n >= p_(t): the first condition is the truncation the method is named for, the second is the one-sided restriction K_s^+, so only an excess of small p-values counts as evidence. Rows whose truncated index set is empty score zero, which is the value the reference implementation's maximum degenerates to.
